newsitem.title: UK: Dollar strong, Euro bourses gain ground.
newsitem.headline: Dollar strong, Euro bourses gain ground.

text.p: The dollar extended its show of strength on Wednesday, while European bourses took their cue from Wall Street to move ahead in early business.

But the U.S. currency and shares later slipped from their highs. A bigger than forecast drop in the British jobless total rekindled fears of higher interest rates and sent the London stock market, Europe's busiest, into the minus column after a higher start.
On the bullion market, gold slipped below expected support at around $338 an ounce. Traders felt that it could weaken some more, hit by strength in the dollar and fears of further selling.

As the U.S. currency hit new 34-month highs against the mark and Swiss franc and made more gains against the yen, currency traders reported market concern that central banks might soon step in to cool things off.
"The central banks are probably thinking about intervening at some point soon," said Stephen King, deputy chief economist at HSBC James Capel.
"It's almost as if they're seeing how far the markets can push the dollar before they take some intervention themselves."
"We're pretty close to levels where the Bank of Japan would be looking to intervene," said Chris Turner, currency strategist at BZW.
The dollar surged to 1.6935 marks, 1.4500 Swiss francs and 124.48 yen, well up from Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6720, 1.4340 and 122.90, before slipping back.
It drew support overnight from reports quoting German finance officials in favour of a rally to 1.70-1.75 marks to trim German export prices and boost the troubled economy.

The German Finance Ministry responded that it had nothing to add to a statement from the weekend meeting of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations that currency "misalignments" had been corrected.

The German Bundesbank weighed in rather more strongly to aid the mark. It said it continued to support the G7 statement, adding: "That statement said the dollar has been corrected and it was made at a rate of 1.65 marks."

Currency traders said Wednesday's second leg of the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding could give the dollar even more support. Further ahead market players are looking to Thursday's U.S. January retail sales data and Friday's producer prices.
More signs of strength in the world's biggest economy could provide additional fuel to ignite the dollar's rally, contrasting with problems in Germany and Japan, analysts said.

The London stock market, already wary over the impact on British companies of a strong pound, lost initial gains after news that unemployment fell 67,800 in January, more than double what economists had expected.

"We've had some disappointing trading statements over the past few weeks. Companies have been blaming sterling for the shortfall and the pound keeps going higher," the head of trading at a key investment bank said.
The strong dollar helped pushed sterling to fresh 52-month highs against the German currency around 2.76 marks versus 2.7480 overnight.
In Frankfurt, shares opened strongly but then came down from their highs.

French shares also edged back after surging one percent higher within 10 minutes of opening, buoyed by Wall Street's gains, the dollar's strength and rising bond markets. French company sales have also been encouraging analysts to upgrade forecasts.
In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average reversed Monday's weak session, rising 51.57 points on Tuesday to close at 6,858.11.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6795 marks and 123.70 yen, compared with 1.6720 and 122.90 in late trading on Tuesday
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
London's FTSE-100 index was down 6.4 points at 4,297.9.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX index was up 23.06 at 3,210.64. In Paris, the CAC-40 was 22.28 higher at 2,604.37.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $336.90 an ounce, down from its close in London on Monday of $339.55. Silver slid to $4.82 from $4.93.
